evidence: const inviteToken = randomBytes(32).toString("hex"); ... await tx.org_users.create({ data: { ... invite_token: inviteToken, password_hash: "" } });
claim_violated: operator subscription lifecycle functions end-to-end; a paying operator can access the product
expected: After Stripe checkout completes and the org/admin user is created, the operator receives a welcome/activation email containing a one-time link to set their password (consuming invite_token), so they can log into /partner.
done_when: checkout.session.completed sends an activation email to the org admin with a tokenized set-password link; following that link sets password_hash and grants first login; verified by a test asserting an email is dispatched and the token is consumable.
completion_hint: In handleCheckoutComplete, after creating org_users, call sendEmail() with a set-password URL keyed on invite_token; add a route that consumes invite_token to set the initial password (mirror password-reset 'reset' action).

evidence: if (meta.userId) { await db.$executeRaw`UPDATE org_users SET setup_token_hash = ${setupTokenHash} ...` } ... return jsonResponse({ ..., tempPassword: meta.tempPassword, ... })
claim_violated: post-checkout the operator is handed a working path into their account
expected: checkout-success returns a usable activation credential. Either meta.userId/meta.tempPassword are populated upstream, or this returns a real setup token the success UI uses.
done_when: the values checkout-success depends on are actually set by the checkout/webhook flow (or the dead setup_token_hash branch and empty tempPassword are removed and replaced with the real invite/activation path); a test proves the returned payload yields a working first login.
completion_hint: meta.userId and meta.tempPassword are never set anywhere (webhook sets neither, create-checkout-session sets neither), so the setup_token_hash UPDATE never runs and tempPassword is always empty. Wire to the invite_token activation flow instead.

done_when: client-invoices GET reads client_invoices (not activity_log) and returns the same invoice shape as client-billing, or this stale endpoint is removed; verified by a test asserting the source table.

evidence: try { switch (event.type) { ... } } catch (err) { ... }  // no record of processed event.id; no idempotency-key store
claim_violated: webhook is idempotent against Stripe's at-least-once redelivery
expected: processed Stripe event ids are recorded/deduped so a redelivered event cannot double-apply a non-idempotent effect.
done_when: the handler records event.id and short-circuits on replay (or each handler is provably idempotent and that is documented/tested).
completion_hint: Org creation is guarded by stripe_customer_id and the updateMany handlers are naturally idempotent, but there is no explicit event-id dedup; add a processed_events table or unique key.

claim_violated: a completed checkout always provisions an org or surfaces a failure
expected: a checkout.session.completed with missing metadata is logged/alerted rather than silently dropped, so a paid customer is never left without an org.
done_when: the early return logs an error and/or captures to Sentry (captureRouteError) with the session id; verified by a test that a metadata-less session triggers an alert.
completion_hint: Our own create-checkout-session always sets metadata, but a Stripe-dashboard or Payment-Link checkout would hit this silent return — paid, no org, no signal.
